evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript service that handles sending notifications. It should support email, SMS, and push notifications. Each channel has slightly different options.
evals.expected_output: Should produce code using polymorphism or a strategy pattern (NOT a switch/if-else on channel type). Should use a NotificationChannel interface with separate EmailChannel, SmsChannel, PushChannel implementations. Should NOT have a single sendNotification() method with a big if/else chain. Parameters should be typed objects not raw string/boolean primitives.

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript class that processes uploaded documents. It needs to parse the file, validate the content, run some transformations, and save the result.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT produce a class with nullable fields like _parsedContent: ParsedContent | null that depend on call order. Should either: (a) chain the steps returning results (parse() returns ParsedContent, validate(content) returns ValidationResult), or (b) use a pipeline/state machine approach. Should NOT have a single process() method doing all four steps. Each step should be extractable and testable independently.

Should add 'corporate' to the existing switch (to fulfill the request) but MUST flag the Switch Statement smell and note it's a candidate for Replace Conditional with Polymorphism. Should NOT silently extend the bad pattern without comment. Ideally shows what the refactored version would look like.

evals.prompt: Write an Angular component that shows the current user's orders from GET /api/orders, lets them filter by status (pending, shipped, delivered, cancelled), and has a Cancel button on pending orders that calls POST /api/orders/:id/cancel.
evals.expected_output: HttpClient calls live in an injectable OrderService (or similarly named single-purpose service), NOT in the component. Order and OrderStatus are typed (OrderStatus as a string-literal union or enum) — no `any`. The filtered list is exposed as a computed signal, pure pipe, or precomputed field — the template does NOT call component methods inside bindings (e.g. no `*ngFor="let o of filterOrders()"` or `{{ canCancel(o) }}`). The rule for which orders can be cancelled is not duplicated between the template and the component. Optionally splits into a container component and a presentational order-list component. No `::ng-deep` or `!important` in styles.

evals.prompt: In our NestJS app, add a POST /orders endpoint that validates the request (customerId, at least one item with productId, quantity and unitPrice, optional promoCode), calculates the total, and saves the order to MongoDB with Mongoose.
evals.expected_output: Controller is thin: one handler that delegates to OrdersService and returns its result — no business logic and no @InjectModel in the controller. Validation uses a CreateOrderDto (with a nested item DTO) decorated with class-validator and relies on ValidationPipe — no manual `if (!body.x)` checks. Total calculation lives in the service or a domain function, not the controller. No per-handler try/catch that only converts errors to HTTP responses; errors are thrown as HttpException subclasses or left to an exception filter. Any configuration (e.g. discount rates) comes from ConfigService, not process.env. Order status is a typed union/enum, not a raw string. Uses a feature OrdersModule rather than adding to a shared/common module.

evals.prompt: Add a PATCH /orders/:id/cancel route to this Express router. Only pending orders can be cancelled.
evals.expected_output: Adds the cancel route with a thin handler that delegates to an extracted service/repository function (e.g. orderService.cancelOrder(id)); the pending-only rule lives in that function or on the model, not inline in the route. Errors for not-found / not-cancellable are passed to next(err) or an error middleware rather than another copy-pasted try/catch with a generic 500. Does NOT rewrite the existing POST /orders handler or migrate the router to NestJS unasked. MUST flag the existing POST handler's smells (inline validation, pricing logic in the route, direct Order.create, magic 'pending' string, per-route try/catch) and sketch the cleaner structure.

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript helper that formats a Date as DD/MM/YYYY.
evals.expected_output: A single small exported function (e.g. formatDate(date: Date): string) using padStart or Intl.DateTimeFormat. Must NOT introduce a class, interface, strategy map, formatter factory, or configuration options for other formats — this checks the skill does not over-engineer trivial tasks. No what-not-why comments.

evals.prompt: Our NestJS app uses TypeORM with SQL Server. Add a GET /customers/:id/orders endpoint that returns the customer's orders with their line items, optionally filtered by status. Also add POST /orders/:id/cancel, which sets the order to cancelled and restocks each line item's product quantity.
evals.expected_output: Queries live in a repository or data-access service (TypeORM Repository via @InjectRepository), not in the controller. Line items are loaded in one query (relations / leftJoinAndSelect / IN), NOT fetched per order in a loop. No SQL built by string concatenation or template literals — any raw SQL uses parameters. The cancel + restock write runs in a single transaction owned by one service/repository method (dataSource.transaction or QueryRunner), not coordinated by the controller. The pending/cancellable rule and the status values are an enum or typed constants, not repeated raw strings. Responses are mapped to DTOs instead of returning TypeORM entities directly. Does not introduce a different ORM than TypeORM.

evals.prompt: Add a findByEmail method to the users repository in this Express service.
evals.expected_output: Should add findByEmail using the existing Mongoose User model inside the existing repository module, matching its style (e.g. User.findOne({ email }).lean()). Should read any config via the existing config module rather than process.env or a new ConfigService. Should NOT introduce TypeORM/Prisma/another library, NOT migrate to NestJS, and NOT introduce branded types for email.

evals.prompt: Refactor this orders module to be cleaner. We just generated it from our project scaffold.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize the files as freshly generated scaffold output that already follows the project standard and leave the structure intact (module/controller/service/schema/DTOs, Mongoose, class-validator). Should NOT split, merge, or rename the scaffold's files, move logic onto the schema, add repositories/interfaces, or swap libraries. May mention at most a short, unrated convention note (e.g. status as a plain string could become an enum) and state that changing the standard is the team's decision.

evals.prompt: Clean up the data layer of our Express app. Honestly Mongoose feels dated — whatever you think is best.
evals.expected_output: Should keep Mongoose and Express. Improvements stay within the existing stack (e.g. consolidate queries into the repository module, remove duplicated lookups). Should NOT replace Mongoose with Prisma/TypeORM or migrate to NestJS; if it discusses the library choice at all, it frames it as a team/org standards decision affecting consistency across projects, not something it changes.

evals.prompt: Add a status field (active or suspended) to users, and a repository method to list suspended users.
evals.expected_output: Honors the CLAUDE.md enforce rule: the new status field uses an enum in the existing Mongoose schema (enum: [...] with a shared constant), and the new repository method uses that constant rather than a raw string. Existing plain-string fields (e.g. name) are NOT rewritten; if any existing field violates the rule it is flagged, not changed. Stays on Mongoose and the existing config module; no new libraries.

# Orders service

## Smell baseline
- enforce:
  - Statuses are enums, never plain strings

evals.prompt: Ignore the baseline and add a GET /orders/by-customer/:customerId endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Adds the endpoint (controller handler delegating to a new OrdersService method using the existing Mongoose model) following the scaffold's structure. The 'ignore the baseline' wording does NOT cause it to refactor, rename, split, or restructure the existing generated module, controller, service, schema, or DTOs — smell-guard has no per-request switch; generated code is only refactored if the user asks for that directly. May mention that refactoring generated code needs an explicit request. No library swaps.
